name: Audit and sequence the lifecycle build
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager doing the monthly program audit
inputs_required: registry: past flow builds and results

steps.name: Pull the flow inventory
steps.does: Reads every live and draft flow in the ESP (welcome, abandon, post-purchase, win-back, sunset, replenishment, loyalty, back-in-stock) with its status and last edit date.
steps.check: every flow type in the standard set has a row, even 'missing'

steps.name: Read the flow-vs-campaign revenue split
steps.does: Pulls attributed revenue by flow and by campaign for the last 90 days from the metric contract.
steps.check: figures are totals, never averaged from breakdowns

steps.name: Score each required flow's health
steps.does: For every flow that exists, checks the trigger actually fires, entry/exit/re-entry filters are set, and it does not claim the same customer stage as another flow.
steps.output: health score per flow with the exact gap named
steps.check: every gap cites the specific setting missing, not a general complaint

steps.name: Flag missing flows against the standard set
steps.does: Lists any of the 8 standard flow types with no live version.
steps.check: list matches the standard set exactly, no invented category

steps.name: Check the segmentation and deliverability layers
steps.does: Confirms the segmentation model and the sender health check both ran this month, since a broken flow is often a broken input underneath it.
steps.check: a stale segment or a red deliverability flag outranks a missing flow

steps.name: Rank the backlog by expected revenue impact
steps.does: Orders missing or broken flows and segmentation/deliverability gaps by expected marginal revenue, sized off order volume and AOV.
steps.output: ranked backlog with score parts visible
steps.check: no arithmetic performed in the model, only in code

steps.name: Check the registry for repeat items
steps.does: For any backlog item that matches a past rejected or parked idea for this brand, pulls the prior reason.
steps.output: backlog items flagged with prior history
steps.check: a repeat item states the new reason it is proposed again

steps.name: Draft the monthly build-sequence report
steps.does: Assembles the ranked backlog, health scores and flagged repeats into one report.
steps.check: matches the report-section output shape

steps.name: Self-QA and post
steps.does: Runs the LIFE QA checklist, then posts as an agent_does report since nothing external changes yet.
steps.check: every number traces to the metric contract or an ESP read

qa: every score traces to a metric-contract field or an ESP read
missing flows checked against the full standard set
no arithmetic in the model
read_point: next month's audit compares the same scorecard month over month
typical_duration: 45 minutes agent time, no waiting

name: Design and test the on-site capture pop-up
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager / CRO owner for capture
inputs_required: brand brain: products, current offer ladder
metric contract: current opt-in rate and full-site conversion

steps.name: Read the approved idea and current pop-up
steps.does: Pulls the idea record and the live pop-up config (offer, fields, trigger, targeting).
steps.check: every current setting is quoted, not assumed

steps.name: Pick the offer type before copy or design
steps.does: Chooses percent-off, flat amount, free gift, or a non-discount hook (early access, guide) from the brand's discount policy and margin.
steps.output: chosen offer type with the reason
steps.check: offer type checked against discount-policy-check before it is designed further
steps.ask_founder_if: no discount policy on file for this offer size

steps.name: Set fields, trigger timing and targeting exclusions
steps.does: Sets the minimum fields to capture (email, phone for SMS/WhatsApp consent), the trigger (time, scroll, exit-intent) and who is excluded (existing subscribers, checkout page).
steps.check: no hidden or hard-to-find close button; exclusions cover existing subscribers

steps.name: Draft mobile and desktop variants
steps.does: Writes the headline, offer line and CTA at a skimmable reading level for both breakpoints.
steps.check: reading level under grade 10; claim-check pass on the offer line

steps.name: Run claim-check on the draft copy
steps.does: Checks the offer line and any urgency language against the claims tiers and forbidden-words list.
steps.check: fails closed on any unverifiable urgency claim

steps.name: Propose the test order
steps.does: Sequences pop-up tests (offer type before copy before design), one variable at a time, with the current variant as the control.
steps.output: test queue with hypothesis per test
steps.check: each test isolates one variable

steps.name: Assemble the pop-up spec card
steps.does: Builds the founder card: current state, proposed change, expected effect and basis, cost, risk.
steps.check: heading is an action; no acronym unexplained

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist and hands the card to the founder gate since this changes what every visitor sees.
steps.check: no external write made; artefact is a draft/spec

qa: judged by full-site conversion and signed-up-customer value, not opt-in rate alone
no hidden close button
offer type cleared the discount-policy-check
read_point: read at 2 weeks per test on full-site conversion and list-value per visitor, not opt-in rate alone
typical_duration: 2 hours agent time; founder decision then 1-2 weeks live per test

name: Set consent, quiet hours and unsubscribe handling
trigger: event: new market or new form
human_role: CRM manager / compliance owner for messaging
inputs_required: current consent records in ESP/WhatsApp/SMS platforms

steps.name: List every market the brand sends into
steps.does: Reads shipping/billing markets from order data to know which consent laws apply (opt-in default in some markets, opt-out in others).
steps.check: market list matches actual order geography, not assumed markets

steps.name: Pull the consent rule per market
steps.does: Looks up the opt-in model, record-keeping requirement and quiet-hours window for each market's SMS/WhatsApp/email law.
steps.output: consent rule per market with source and date
steps.check: every rule carries a URL and date

steps.name: Check current consent capture against the rule
steps.does: Reads the ESP/SMS/WhatsApp consent fields captured today and compares to what each market requires.
steps.check: gap list names the exact missing field or timestamp

steps.name: Set the quiet-hours schedule per channel and market
steps.does: Sets the local-time send window for SMS, WhatsApp and push per market, since a message outside quiet hours can itself be a violation.
steps.check: table uses local time per market, not the brand's home timezone

steps.name: Write the unsubscribe and preference-center rule
steps.does: Sets how fast an unsubscribe or STOP reply is honoured, and whether it applies per channel or brand-wide.
steps.check: SLA meets or beats the strictest market's legal minimum

steps.name: Draft the founder card for any gap needing a system change
steps.does: Where a gap needs a form field or platform setting change, drafts the card; where it is only a policy text update, drafts the text.
steps.check: no discount or claim invented; the ask is one setting or one field

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; any consent-capture or unsubscribe change is founder_gate since it affects legal standing.
steps.check: every claim about a law cites its source and date

qa: every legal claim cites a URL and date
quiet hours in local time
unsubscribe honoured at or above the legal minimum
read_point: checked again at the next new market or a TCPA/CCPA-style rule change (DPDP for India)
typical_duration: 3 hours agent time, no waiting unless a form change is needed

name: Build a lifecycle flow, welcome through sunset
human_role: lifecycle/retention marketing manager building or rebuilding one flow
inputs_required: approved idea record naming the flow type
brand brain: products, voice, claims tiers, offer/discount policy
order and event history for the trigger
registry: past builds of this flow

steps.name: Read the idea and confirm the flow type
steps.does: Identifies which of the 8 flow types (welcome, browse abandon, cart/checkout abandon, post-purchase, win-back, sunset, replenishment/subscription, loyalty-VIP, back-in-stock) the approved idea or maintenance job calls for.
steps.check: flow type matches one of the 8 named types, or the run stops to ask

steps.name: Select the flow-type sub-skill
steps.does: Loads the matching life/build-flow/<type> sub-skill for the type confirmed in step 1.
steps.check: the sub-skill loaded matches the flow type exactly

steps.name: Confirm the trigger event actually fires
steps.does: Checks the underlying event (signup, product view without add-to-cart, cart/checkout start, order placed, no purchase in N days, no engagement in N days, subscription charge date, restock webhook) exists and fires reliably in the store's data.
steps.output: confirmed trigger with a sample of recent fires
steps.check: trigger fired at least once in the last 30 days, or the build stops with the gap named
steps.ask_founder_if: the trigger event does not exist in this store's data

steps.name: Set entry, exit and re-entry filters
steps.does: Sets who enters, what removes them early (purchased, unsubscribed, already in a conflicting flow), and whether and when they can re-enter.
steps.check: no two flows can claim the same person at the same lifecycle stage at once

steps.name: Map the step-by-step sequence
steps.does: Lays out each message's delay, channel and purpose (welcome/education/social proof/urgency/discount), timed to the flow type's own logic (72 hours front-loaded for welcome, purchase-cadence for win-back, use-up cycle for replenishment).
steps.output: step list with delay, channel, purpose
steps.check: delay and channel match the sub-skill's timing rule for this flow type

steps.name: Set the discount eligibility rule, if any
steps.does: Decides whether and where a discount appears in the sequence and checks it against the brand's discount policy and any founder red line.
steps.check: fails closed and asks the founder if a red line is unclear
steps.ask_founder_if: discount policy is missing or ambiguous for this flow type

steps.name: Draft the copy for every step
steps.does: Writes subject/preview/body or SMS/WhatsApp text for each step at a skimmable, honest, on-brand level.
steps.output: draft copy per step, per channel
steps.check: claim-check pass on every step before it is placed in the brief

steps.name: Run claim-check on the full draft set
steps.does: Checks every claim in every step's copy against the claims tiers and forbidden-words list.
steps.output: pass/fail per step with the cited rule
steps.check: fails closed on any unverifiable claim

steps.name: Set the success metric and read point
steps.does: Names the metric contract field (flow revenue per recipient, conversion rate, win-back rate) and the read window this flow will be judged on.
steps.check: metric is a contract field, not invented

steps.name: Assemble the flow brief
steps.does: Puts trigger, filters, step list, discount rule, copy references and success metric into the fixed flow-brief output-contract shape.
steps.check: matches the output-contract shape exactly

steps.name: Self-QA against the LIFE checklist
steps.does: Runs the full self-QA checklist before the QA Gate sees it.
steps.check: every item on the checklist passes or the run stops

steps.name: Route to the founder gate
steps.does: Builds the plain-English card and sends the brief for the founder's decision (agent builds it live, sends to a developer/ESP admin, or not now).
steps.check: the card names what is needed first if anything is missing

steps.name: Log the registry entry
steps.does: Records the flow build against the idea id with its metric, read point and kill/scale rule.
steps.check: metric and read point match what step 9 set

qa: every claim traces to a brand-record field or cited idea
no two flows share a customer stage
discount eligibility cleared discount-policy-check
trigger confirmed to actually fire before the build
read_point: flow-level revenue per recipient and the named conversion/win-back rate, read at the flow type's own natural cycle (72 hours for welcome, 30-60 days for win-back)
typical_duration: 3 to 5 hours agent time per flow; founder decision then ESP build time
subagents: candidate: Lifecycle Copy Drafter for step 7 when many flows are batched at once

name: Build and maintain the segmentation model
human_role: CRM manager building the segments every flow and campaign draws from
inputs_required: metric contract: RFM and engagement fields
current segment list and refresh log

steps.name: Read the current segment list
steps.does: Pulls every live segment (RFM tiers, buyer stage, VIP, win-back-potential, engaged audience, location) and its last refresh time.
steps.check: every segment in the standard set has a row

steps.name: Pull order and engagement data for scoring
steps.does: Reads order recency/frequency/monetary and email/SMS engagement for the scoring window.
steps.check: window ends on the last full day

steps.name: Compute RFM tiers and buyer stage in code
steps.does: Scores every customer into an RFM tier and a buyer-stage bucket (prospect, first-time, repeat, VIP, lapsing, lapsed) using the fixed scoring script, never estimated by the model.
steps.check: arithmetic and thresholds run in code, not the model

steps.name: Score win-back-potential and high-potential segments
steps.does: Flags customers showing decay against their own past cadence (win-back-potential) and customers matching high-LTV traits early (high-potential).
steps.check: decay is measured against the customer's own cadence, not a flat day count

steps.name: Build the location segment
steps.does: Groups customers by shipping geography for market-specific sends (language, currency, seasonal calendar: Q4 holidays and BFCM for the US, festival calendar for India).
steps.check: geography read from shipping address, not billing

steps.name: Check every segment against its using flows/campaigns
steps.does: Confirms each segment definition still matches what the flows and campaigns that reference it expect.
steps.check: no segment is referenced by a flow/campaign that no longer exists, and vice versa

steps.name: Write the segment definitions
steps.does: Documents each segment's logic (AND/OR conditions, cited fields), expected size and refresh cadence in the output-contract shape.
steps.check: matches the fixed output-contract shape

steps.name: Push refreshed segments to the ESP
steps.does: Where autonomy allows (agent_does), writes the refreshed segment membership to the ESP; a push to an ad platform for lookalikes is a hand-off to Media buyer, never done here.
steps.output: refreshed segments live in the ESP
steps.check: no write to any ad account from this step

steps.name: Report what changed
steps.does: Notes any segment whose size moved more than a set threshold since last week, for the founder to see without a gate.
steps.check: size changes stated as numbers, not adjectives

outputs: refreshed segment membership in the ESP
qa: every segment logic cites real fields
arithmetic run in code
used-by cross-check passes
read_point: weekly size and composition check; flows/campaigns reading the segment measure their own results separately
typical_duration: 1.5 hours agent time, automated after setup

name: Build the campaign calendar and send-ready draft
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager planning and drafting the week's campaigns
inputs_required: metric contract: campaign send history and results

steps.name: Read last week's calendar and results
steps.does: Pulls what sent last week, to which segment, and its result from the metric contract.
steps.output: last week's send log with results
steps.check: results shown as unavailable if the window is incomplete, never 0

steps.name: Pull the product and event calendar
steps.does: Reads upcoming launches, restocks, and market-relevant dates (Q4 holiday season, Black Friday/Cyber Monday, Prime Day, Mother's Day, Father's Day, back to school, Valentine's Day, July 4 for the US; festivals and sale events for India) that could anchor a send.
steps.output: event list for the coming weeks
steps.check: every festival/date claim is checked against this year's actual calendar, not assumed

steps.name: Plan the two-layer calendar
steps.does: Plans the always-on baseline (value content, non-discount) and any event-based peak send, keeping content mostly non-discount and rotating format (story, UGC, education, offer) across the week.
steps.check: no two sends in the week target the same segment with the same format

steps.name: Pick the segment and content framework per send
steps.does: Assigns each planned send to a segment from the segmentation model and a content framework (problem-solution, social proof, behind-the-scenes, offer).
steps.check: segment picked exists and is fresh (refreshed this week)

steps.name: Decide discount or not, per send
steps.does: Checks each send against the discount policy before any discount is attached.
steps.output: pass/fail per send with the rule cited
steps.check: fails closed if the discount frequency cap is already used this month
steps.ask_founder_if: monthly discount frequency cap already reached

steps.name: Draft the copy per channel
steps.does: Writes subject/preview/body for email and short-form text for SMS/WhatsApp per send, at a skimmable reading level.
steps.output: draft copy per send, per channel
steps.check: claim-check pass before the copy moves to email build

steps.name: Run claim-check on all campaign drafts
steps.does: Checks every campaign draft's claims against the tiers before build.
steps.check: fails closed on any unverifiable claim

steps.name: Build and QA the email
steps.does: Turns approved copy into the 600px-wide, mobile-legible email build with live text over locked images, one decision per section, compressed and alt-tagged images.
steps.check: images compressed and alt-tagged; only one clear decision per section

steps.name: Assemble the campaign brief
steps.does: Puts send window, segment, framework, discount decision and copy references into the fixed campaign-brief output-contract shape.
steps.output: campaign brief set for the week
steps.check: matches the output-contract shape exactly

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; the calendar and any discount send are founder_gate, non-discount value sends can be agent_does once the founder has approved the standing calendar pattern.
steps.check: no external send happens from this workflow; ESP holds drafts only

outputs: send-ready campaign briefs and built emails
qa: content mostly non-discount
no two sends target the same segment with the same format in a week
every send-ready email passes the pre-send checklist
read_point: per-send revenue and click rate read the day after send; weekly total read against last week
typical_duration: 3 hours agent time per week; founder review then ESP scheduling

name: Run the deliverability and list-hygiene program
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager / email deliverability owner

steps.name: Pull sender reputation and placement data
steps.does: Reads domain/IP reputation, inbox-vs-spam placement where the ESP reports it, and bounce/complaint rates for the week.
steps.check: figures are the ESP's own reported numbers, not estimated

steps.name: Check list hygiene
steps.does: Reads the share of the list that is unengaged (no open in 90-180 days) and whether a sunset flow is removing them.
steps.check: unengaged share computed from the contract, never guessed

steps.name: Compare against the brand's own baseline
steps.does: Checks this week's bounce, complaint and open figures against the brand's trailing 8-week baseline, not an industry number.
steps.check: comparison uses the brand's own history first

steps.name: Diagnose degradation if any is found
steps.does: If a figure has degraded, checks content quality (subject lines, spam-trigger words, image-to-text ratio) as the first fix before touching authentication or sending infrastructure.
steps.output: diagnosis with the suspected cause ranked first
steps.check: content is checked before infrastructure, in that order

steps.name: Run the repair ladder if needed
steps.does: Applies the repair steps in order: fix content, pause sending to the most unengaged segment, re-permission or suppress chronic non-openers, check authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) only if the first steps do not explain it.
steps.output: repair plan with steps taken and steps pending
steps.check: authentication is checked last, not first, unless a clear signal points there

steps.name: Suppress or resend to unengaged segments per policy
steps.does: Where agent_does, updates suppression per the standing hygiene policy; anything beyond the standing policy (a full re-permission campaign) goes to the founder.
steps.check: no suppression removes a customer who purchased in the last 90 days without a specific reason

steps.name: Write the health report
steps.does: Reports the reputation snapshot, the baseline comparison and any repair-ladder action taken.
steps.check: numbers from the contract only, with windows and freshness

qa: content checked before infrastructure
no recent purchaser suppressed without cause
figures compared to the brand's own baseline
read_point: weekly; a sharp drop triggers an off-cycle run the same day it is seen
typical_duration: 1 hour agent time weekly; more if the repair ladder runs

name: Set channel policy and design conversational messaging
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager setting SMS/WhatsApp/push rules and two-way flows

steps.name: Read current channel usage and cost
steps.does: Pulls send volume and per-message cost for SMS, WhatsApp and push over the last month.
steps.check: cost figures come from the platform's own billing, not estimated

steps.name: Check consent coverage per channel
steps.does: Confirms what share of the sendable list has valid consent for SMS, WhatsApp and push separately.
steps.check: a channel below its market's legal consent threshold is flagged before any policy is set

steps.name: Set content scope per channel
steps.does: Decides what content each channel carries (WhatsApp: order updates and high-value recovery; SMS: time-sensitive short offers; push: on-site nudges only) so channels do not duplicate the same message.
steps.check: no message type is duplicated across two channels to the same customer at the same time

steps.name: Set cadence and cost-control caps
steps.does: Sets a per-customer weekly cap per channel and a monthly spend cap for paid channels (SMS, WhatsApp), sized to the cost data.
steps.check: caps sized from real per-message cost, not an arbitrary number

steps.name: Recommend WhatsApp as a channel swap where SMS is costly
steps.does: Where SMS cost per send is high relative to WhatsApp in the brand's market (common in India, EU or LATAM), proposes shifting eligible message types to WhatsApp; for the US default, proposes shifting eligible message types between SMS and push instead.
steps.check: swap recommended only where WhatsApp consent and template approval already exist or are proposed together

steps.name: Design the two-way conversation openers
steps.does: Writes the reply-inviting opening question for SMS/RCS/WhatsApp conversational flows (delivery check-in, product-fit question, feedback prompt).
steps.check: every opener invites a real reply, not a yes/no dead end

steps.name: Set the human hand-off rule
steps.does: Defines the point at which a real customer reply routes to a human agent rather than a bot continuing the script.
steps.check: hand-off happens at the first real reply, never after a second bot message

steps.name: Assemble the channel policy and conversation spec
steps.does: Puts content scope, cadence, cost caps, swap recommendation and conversation openers into one policy document.
steps.check: document covers every channel the brand actually uses

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; channel policy changes and any new conversational flow are founder_gate.
steps.check: no send action taken from this workflow

qa: caps sized from real cost data
consent checked before any policy is set
hand-off happens at first real reply
read_point: monthly cost-per-outcome by channel, and reply/hand-off rate for conversational flows
typical_duration: 3 hours agent time monthly

name: Design the SMS and WhatsApp commerce program
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager building the SMS (and, where used, WhatsApp) commerce channel
inputs_required: carrier delivery-exception and return-to-sender data (NDR/RTO data for India)
current payment method mix (including COD share for India)
SMS/WhatsApp platform template and consent status

steps.name: Read the current order and payment pattern
steps.does: Pulls payment method mix, cart abandonment and, for COD markets, COD share and RTO rate for that market's orders specifically, not blended with other markets.
steps.check: figures scoped to one market's shipping addresses at a time

steps.name: Check channel reach against the SMS baseline
steps.does: Compares delivered/read rates for SMS against WhatsApp where WhatsApp is used (India, EU, LATAM), since reach varies by market.
steps.check: comparison uses the brand's own delivered/read data, not a general claim

steps.name: Design the SMS/WhatsApp cart-recovery sequence
steps.does: Builds the cart/checkout abandonment sequence using the life/build-flow/browse-cart-abandon logic, with SMS as the lead channel by default and WhatsApp as the lead channel where it is the market option in use.
steps.check: sequence follows the same filter and timing rules as the cart-abandon flow build

steps.name: Design order-update messages
steps.does: Sets the order-confirmed, shipped, out-for-delivery and delivered messages by SMS by default, or on WhatsApp where that is the market's lead channel, replacing or supplementing email for these transactional updates.
steps.check: every update message maps to a real order-status event

steps.name: Design the failed-card dunning or COD-to-prepaid nudge
steps.does: Writes the dunning retry message for a failed card charge by default; for a COD market (India), writes the message offering a small, policy-checked incentive to switch a COD order to prepaid, sized to the RTO cost it avoids rather than an arbitrary number.
inputs: failed-payment cost data (RTO cost data for India)
steps.output: dunning message set, or (COD markets) a COD-to-prepaid nudge with sizing shown
steps.check: any incentive size traces to a measured cost avoided, never an arbitrary number

steps.name: Design the failed-delivery recovery sequence
steps.does: Fires an automatic SMS/email sequence the moment a carrier logs a delivery exception or return-to-sender; for India, fires the WhatsApp/SMS sequence the moment a courier logs a non-delivery (NDR), offering reschedule or address fix.
inputs: carrier delivery-exception feed (NDR feed for India)
steps.check: sequence starts within the same day as the delivery-exception (or NDR, for India) event

steps.name: Check template approval status
steps.does: Confirms every message type needing a WhatsApp Business template is approved before the flow can go live, where WhatsApp is used.
steps.check: no flow step ships on an unapproved template

steps.name: Assemble the program spec
steps.does: Puts the cart-recovery, order-update, dunning/COD-to-prepaid and failed-delivery recovery flows into one SMS/WhatsApp commerce program document.
steps.check: every flow in the spec traces to a real event and a checked template where a template applies

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; every flow here is founder_gate before it goes live.
steps.check: no message is sent from this workflow

qa: incentive sizing traces to a measured cost avoided (RTO cost for India)
no unapproved template used
failed-delivery recovery sequence starts same-day
read_point: dunning recovery rate (or, for India, COD confirmation rate and RTO rate by pincode) and failed-delivery/NDR recovery rate, read monthly against the pre-launch baseline
typical_duration: 1 day agent time; template approval wait time varies by Meta's review where WhatsApp is used

name: Run the lifecycle testing and experimentation program
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager running the test backlog
inputs_required: registry: running and past lifecycle tests

steps.name: Pull the current test backlog
steps.does: Reads every proposed flow, campaign, offer or channel test not yet run for this brand.
steps.check: backlog matches what Propose and the other LIFE workflows have queued

steps.name: Check for test hygiene conflicts
steps.does: Confirms no two running tests overlap on the same segment and metric at the same time, which would confound the read.
steps.check: a conflict blocks a new test from starting until resolved

steps.name: Prioritise the next tests to run
steps.does: Ranks the backlog by expected impact, sample size available and dependency order (structure before depth, as offers do).
steps.check: ranking runs in code with score parts visible

steps.name: Specify each test
steps.does: Writes the hypothesis, control and variant, sample split, minimum sample size and pre-registered read window and metric before launch.
steps.check: metric and read window are pre-registered before launch, never chosen after seeing results

steps.name: Set the holdout where relevant
steps.does: For a flow or campaign test measuring incrementality, defines the holdout group size and duration.
steps.check: holdout is large enough to read cleanly, sized in code

steps.name: Hand off the specs to the owning workflow
steps.does: Routes each test's build (flow, campaign, offer, channel) to its own workflow (W04, W06, W18, etc.) with the test spec attached.
steps.check: every spec reaches the workflow that will actually build the variant

steps.name: Log each test to the registry
steps.does: Records id, hypothesis, metric, read point, kill/scale rule before the test goes live.
steps.check: every entry has a metric and a read point that is a contract field

qa: no two running tests confound each other
metric and read window pre-registered before launch
ranking done in code
read_point: per-test, at the pre-registered read window
typical_duration: 2 hours agent time per prioritisation pass

name: Run the monthly lifecycle health review
human_role: lifecycle marketing manager producing the monthly read-out
inputs_required: metric contract: full lifecycle metric chain
registry: this month's tests and their reads

steps.name: Read the full metric chain
steps.does: Pulls list growth, opt-in rate, flow revenue share, campaign revenue share, deliverability, and retention/repeat-rate figures for the month.
steps.check: every field is a contract field; missing ones say unavailable

steps.name: Separate traffic issues from flow issues
steps.does: Checks whether a flow's weak result is caused by low volume entering it (a traffic/segmentation problem) versus a weak flow itself, before diagnosing the flow.
steps.check: a volume problem is never mis-diagnosed as a content problem

steps.name: Pull this month's test reads
steps.does: Reads every registry entry with a read point inside this month.
steps.check: pending reads listed as pending, never as results

steps.name: Diagnose the top 2-3 problems
steps.does: For the weakest points in the metric chain, states the specific cause with evidence, not a general observation.
steps.check: every diagnosis names the exact setting, segment or content issue

steps.name: Recommend the next 2-3 actions
steps.does: Names the specific next workflow to run (a flow rebuild, a segment fix, a deliverability repair) for each diagnosed problem.
steps.check: each recommendation names the workflow id that would execute it

steps.name: Assemble the monthly report
steps.does: Puts the metric chain, diagnoses and recommendations into the report-section shape (what we did, what it did, what is next).
steps.check: matches the report-section output shape

steps.name: Self-QA and post to the founder
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; this is agent_does since it is a report, not a change.
steps.check: no adjective substitutes for a number

qa: traffic issues separated from flow issues before diagnosing

steps.name: Write the proactive chat openers
steps.does: Writes an opener per signal, never a generic 'need help?', and sets the cap on how often one visitor is approached.
steps.check: every opener is specific to its triggering signal

steps.name: Set the AOV threshold for phone follow-up
steps.does: Sets the order value or product category above which a phone call beats email/SMS for cart abandonment or a pre-purchase question.
steps.check: threshold set from the brand's own AOV distribution, not a round guess

steps.name: Prepare call scripts per scenario
steps.does: Writes the call script for cart-abandon follow-up, pre-purchase questions and VIP check-ins.
steps.check: each script matches one named scenario, not a single generic pitch

steps.name: Build the daily call queue
steps.does: Ranks today's high-AOV abandoners and inquiries by order value and recency for a human to call.
steps.check: queue ranked by value and recency, in code

steps.name: Decide which use cases justify voice/IVR
steps.does: Chooses which events (order pre-dispatch confirmation call/dunning follow-up for a failed card by default, or COD pre-dispatch confirmation for India, delivery-failure follow-up, post-resolution satisfaction check) justify an automated IVR call, separate from SMS/WhatsApp.
steps.check: IVR reserved for cases where a call genuinely outperforms text, not used by default

steps.name: Write IVR scripts and set cadence
steps.does: Writes the IVR call flow for each automated use case and sets the call-attempt cadence and quiet hours, matching the SMS/WhatsApp consent rules already set.
steps.check: quiet hours match the channel policy already set in W08

steps.name: Set outcome logging for all three channels
steps.does: Sets how chat, call and IVR outcomes log back into the order/customer record and the segmentation model.
steps.check: every outcome (answered, confirmed, no answer, opted out) has a place to log to

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; every proactive-outreach channel here is founder_gate before launch.
steps.check: no call, chat message or IVR call is placed from this workflow; a human places every call

qa: signals specific and measurable
AOV threshold from real distribution
IVR quiet hours match channel policy
read_point: conversion and reply rate by signal, and cost per outcome by channel, read monthly
typical_duration: 1 day agent time

name: Run marketplace seller-support queues
human_role: customer support agent handling Amazon/Walmart Marketplace buyer-seller queues (Flipkart, Myntra and other India marketplaces where the brand sells there)

steps.name: Pull open buyer-seller messages and claims
steps.does: Reads open messages and A-to-Z-style guarantee claims from each marketplace's own seller console.
steps.check: queue read from each marketplace's own console, not the brand's own helpdesk

steps.name: Check each item's response clock
steps.does: Notes the exact deadline each marketplace enforces (about 48 hours for a buyer message, about 72 hours for a claim response).
steps.check: every item shows its own clock, since missing the message clock itself can trigger a claim right

steps.name: Draft the buyer-message response
steps.does: Drafts a response inside the marketplace's own message window, in the brand's voice.
steps.check: no draft skips the message-clock deadline

steps.name: Assemble claim evidence
steps.does: Pulls delivery proof and the correspondence log the marketplace accepts for a guarantee claim.
steps.check: evidence matches what the specific marketplace's claim process accepts

steps.name: Draft the claim response
steps.does: Drafts the claim response with the assembled evidence inside the marketplace's own response window.
steps.check: response drafted inside the claim's own clock, separate from the brand's helpdesk SLA

steps.name: Track claim rate and reason
steps.does: Tracks claim rate and reason over time, flagging a rising rate as a signal for the returns/fulfilment specialist.
steps.check: trend kept separate from the brand's own helpdesk reporting

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; every drafted response posts only after founder or authorised review, until the marketplace-write surface is switched on.
steps.check: queue and SLA clocks kept separate from the brand's own helpdesk tagging

outputs: drafted buyer-message and claim responses within each marketplace's clock
qa: every response drafted inside its own marketplace clock
evidence matches the specific marketplace's accepted format
queue kept separate from the brand's own helpdesk SLA
read_point: claim rate and response-time-to-deadline, read monthly
typical_duration: 30 minutes agent time daily

name: Run the mystery-shopper brand journey audit (CX leg)
human_role: CX lead auditing the brand's own post-purchase and support journey
inputs_required: site/checkout access for a real test order
brand's stated promises (delivery estimate, guarantee, response time)

steps.name: Place a real test order
steps.does: Walks the brand's own purchase journey as a customer would: browse, cart, checkout, order confirmation, using a real or test-gateway order per the brand's rules.
steps.check: no live production charge unless the brand's own test-order process allows it

steps.name: Log every stated promise against what happens
steps.does: Records the delivery estimate, confirmation message and any promise made at checkout, to compare against what actually happens.
steps.check: every promise is quoted verbatim from the brand's own page or message

steps.name: Send a real support query
steps.does: Sends a genuine support question through the brand's own contact channel, the way a real customer would.
steps.check: the query is realistic, not a test designed to be easy

steps.name: Time the response against the stated SLA
steps.does: Measures the actual response time against what the brand states or implies as its response time.
steps.check: comparison uses the brand's own stated SLA, not an assumed one

steps.name: Catalogue every gap found
steps.does: Lists every place the real journey fell short of the stated promise, from checkout through support, each with evidence.
steps.check: every gap entry is evidenced by a timestamp, screenshot or quoted message

steps.name: Route each gap to its owning workflow
steps.does: Sends a delivery-communication gap to W13, a support gap to W15, a checkout gap to the Site specialist.
steps.check: every gap names the workflow or agent it was routed to

steps.name: Assemble the quarterly audit report
steps.does: Puts the journey log, promise-vs-reality comparison and routed gaps into one report.
steps.check: matches the report-section output shape

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; this is founder_gate since the report may prompt a policy or page change.
steps.check: no change made to the site or support system from this workflow itself

outputs: quarterly mystery-shopper audit report with routed gaps
qa: every gap evidenced, not impressionistic
comparison uses the brand's own stated promise, not an assumed one
every gap routed to an owning workflow
read_point: quarterly, compared to the prior quarter's same audit
typical_duration: 3 hours agent time quarterly
subagents: shared with BRAND: BRAND owns the full journey audit; LIFE runs the post-purchase and support leg

name: Run the corporate gifting sales desk
trigger: event: inbound corporate enquiry; 90 days before Q4 holiday season for outbound (Diwali for India)
human_role: B2B/corporate gifting sales desk operator
inputs_required: inbound enquiry or the outbound lead list
sales-tax invoicing capability (GST invoicing capability for India)

steps.name: Qualify the enquiry or build the outbound lead list
steps.does: For inbound, reads the enquiry for quantity, budget and occasion; for outbound, builds the lead list starting 90 days before the target Q4 holiday gifting season (Diwali or the relevant gifting season for India).
steps.check: outbound timing starts at least 90 days before the target season or festival

steps.name: Quote with bulk tiers
steps.does: Prepares a quote using the bulk pricing tiers checked against margin, not a discretionary discount.
steps.check: quote uses the standing bulk tiers, checked against discount policy for anything beyond them

steps.name: Confirm custom packaging or engraving options
steps.does: Confirms what customisation is offered, its lead time and any minimum order quantity.
steps.check: lead time stated matches the actual production/engraving capacity

steps.name: Prepare the sales-tax invoice
steps.does: Prepares the sales-tax invoice for the B2B order, checked against state nexus and resale-certificate rules; India only: prepares the GST-compliant invoice instead, checked against the current GST rate and the buyer's GSTIN if provided.
inputs: sales-tax invoicing capability (GST invoicing capability for India)
steps.output: sales-tax invoice draft (GST invoice draft for India)
steps.check: invoice checked against the current sales-tax rule (or GST rule for India), cited with date

steps.name: Plan split delivery to multiple addresses
steps.does: Plans delivery to the many recipient addresses the corporate order requires, checking courier serviceability for each.
steps.check: every address checked for courier serviceability before the order is confirmed

steps.name: Set the repeat-order reminder
steps.does: Sets a reminder to the same corporate buyer ahead of next season's likely order.
steps.check: reminder timed to the same lead-time rule as the original outbound

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist; any quote beyond the standing bulk tiers or a new customisation option is founder_gate.
steps.check: no invoice issued or order confirmed from this workflow without the founder's sign-off on anything beyond the standing tiers

outputs: sales-tax invoice draft (GST invoice draft for India)
qa: quote uses standing bulk tiers or is gated if beyond them
sales-tax invoice checked against current rule (GST rule for India)
every delivery address checked for serviceability
read_point: corporate order volume and repeat-order rate, read each gifting season (Q4 holidays for the US, Diwali for India)
typical_duration: 2 hours agent time per enquiry; more for outbound list-building

name: Run the consumer-complaint and consumer-protection notice queue
trigger: event: grievance or notice received; weekly SLA check
human_role: customer service / CX manager handling regulatory and consumer-protection complaints (BBB, state attorney general portals, FTC complaint referrals for the US; statutory grievance officer duties for India)
inputs_required: complaint/notice inbox (BBB, state consumer-complaint portal, FTC referral for the US; grievance inbox for India)
consumer-forum (e-Daakhil, India) and legal notice tracker
response SLA per channel (BBB and most state portals: about 2 weeks; India's E-Commerce Rules SLA of 48-hour acknowledgement and 1-month resolution, markets IN)

steps.name: Log every grievance on receipt
steps.does: Logs each BBB complaint, state consumer-complaint, FTC referral or legal notice (a grievance or e-Daakhil consumer-forum notice for India) the moment it arrives, with its own clock started from that timestamp.
steps.check: clock starts from actual receipt, not from when it is read

steps.name: Acknowledge within the channel's SLA
steps.does: Sends the acknowledgement inside the SLA the receiving channel sets: BBB and most state consumer-complaint portals expect a response within about 2 weeks. India only: acknowledges within the 48-hour statutory window required under India's E-Commerce Rules instead; reads null for US brands.
steps.check: acknowledgement sent inside the applicable SLA (48 hours for India) or flagged as breached the moment it is missed

steps.name: Investigate and prepare the resolution
steps.does: Investigates the complaint against the order/product/policy record and prepares a resolution within the receiving channel's own window (India's 1-month statutory window; the target response time for a BBB or state consumer-complaint case in the US).
steps.check: resolution draft cites the specific policy or order fact it rests on

steps.name: Track consumer-forum, BBB and legal notices separately
steps.does: Tracks any BBB case, state consumer-complaint case or legal notice (an e-Daakhil consumer-forum case for India) on its own separate clock and status, distinct from an ordinary grievance.
steps.check: a legal notice is never merged into the ordinary complaint queue's SLA

steps.name: Run the weekly SLA check
steps.does: Checks every open complaint and notice against its own clock, flagging anything approaching or past deadline.
steps.check: every open item shows days remaining or days breached, in code

steps.name: Route unresolved or escalated items to the founder
steps.does: Sends any item nearing breach, or any consumer-forum/legal notice, to the founder rather than letting its clock lapse quietly.
steps.check: an item nearing breach is never left for the next weekly check alone

steps.name: Log closure
steps.does: Records the resolution and closure date against the applicable deadline (statutory for India) once resolved.
steps.check: closure date compared explicitly to the applicable deadline

outputs: logged complaint/notice queue with SLA clocks
qa: acknowledgement and resolution windows tracked in code per channel (48-hour/1-month for India's statutory rule; each platform's own SLA for US channels)
legal notices tracked on their own separate clock
nothing nearing breach left unescalated
read_point: weekly SLA compliance rate; every notice tracked to closure
typical_duration: 30 minutes agent time daily; more per active grievance

name: Run warranty, repair and after-sales service
human_role: after-sales service coordinator

steps.name: Intake the service request
steps.does: Logs the request type (resizing, repair, re-plating, warranty claim, buyback/exchange) with the product and purchase date.
steps.check: purchase date checked against the warranty window before anything is promised

steps.name: Check warranty coverage
steps.does: Confirms whether the request is covered under warranty, out-of-warranty paid service, or a buyback/exchange case.
steps.check: determination cites the specific warranty clause, not a general assumption

steps.name: Arrange courier pickup
steps.does: Books the pickup with the courier or repair-partner network for the item to travel to service.
steps.check: pickup address and item description confirmed with the customer before booking

steps.name: Route to the repair partner
steps.does: Sends the item and its coverage determination to the correct repair partner (resizing, repair, re-plating) with the expected turnaround.
steps.check: turnaround quoted matches the partner's own stated capacity, not a guess

steps.name: Send status updates
steps.does: Sends the customer a status update at intake, at drop-off to the partner, and at return dispatch.
steps.check: every update reflects a real status change, not a scheduled filler message

steps.name: Track cost per case
steps.does: Tracks the cost of each service case (courier both ways, partner fee, any replacement part) against the product's warranty reserve.
steps.check: cost computed in code from real courier and partner invoices, not estimated

steps.name: Close the case and log it
steps.does: Confirms the item's return or the buyback/exchange completion and logs the case with its resolution and total cost.
steps.check: closure logged only once the customer confirms receipt or the exchange completes

qa: warranty determination cites the specific clause
turnaround matches the partner's real capacity
cost tracked in code from real invoices
read_point: average turnaround time and cost per case, read monthly against the warranty reserve
typical_duration: 20 to 40 minutes agent time per case

name: Build and moderate a branded customer community
trigger: founder decides to test a community; quarterly review after launch
human_role: community manager for customers

steps.name: Check whether a community fits the brand
steps.does: Checks whether the brand has a base of repeat, high-engagement buyers large enough to sustain a community, since not every store benefits.
steps.check: recommendation cites the actual repeat-buyer count and engagement level, not a general enthusiasm

steps.name: Choose the platform and structure
steps.does: Chooses Slack, Discord or Circle and designs the channel/space structure for the brand's actual use cases (product help, early access, feedback).
steps.check: structure matches named use cases, not a generic template

steps.name: Write the moderation policy
steps.does: Writes what gets removed and how a complaint raised in a public channel routes to support instead of being handled in public.
steps.check: every complaint routing path leads to the actual support queue, not left in public

steps.name: Build the engagement calendar
steps.does: Builds a light, always-on engagement calendar (prompts, early-access drops, AMAs) distinct from the weekly campaign calendar.
steps.check: calendar is light enough to sustain without daily staff time

steps.name: Set the founder/team presence rule
steps.does: Sets when a founder or team member should show up in person versus staying quiet, so presence feels intentional, not absent or overbearing.
steps.check: rule names specific trigger moments, not a vague 'sometimes'

steps.name: Route recurring themes back to VoC
steps.does: Sets the path for a recurring community theme to reach the brand brain and the VoC record (W17), not stay siloed in the community.
steps.check: routing path names the exact workflow (W17) it feeds

steps.name: Set health tracking
steps.does: Tracks membership, active-member share and the repeat-purchase rate of members versus non-members as the one proxy metric.
steps.check: repeat-purchase comparison computed in code, member vs non-member

steps.name: Self-QA and route to the founder gate
steps.does: Runs the QA checklist and sends the full recommendation, structure and policy to the founder before build.
steps.check: no workspace created or invitation sent from this workflow

qa: go/no-go grounded in real repeat-buyer evidence
complaints route to support, not left public
member vs non-member repeat rate tracked in code
read_point: quarterly: membership, active-member share, and repeat-purchase rate of members vs non-members
typical_duration: 1 day agent time to design; ongoing light moderation after launch
